text:
Alex: Kicking off ramp tests for LON5 cluster now. Nodepool applied (32x A100, mixed MIG disabled). Target: 8k qps baseline for model-serving. Please run the quick acceptance checklist: network egress, NTP, KMS, GPU drivers, autoscaler, nvlink, prefix cache.
Mira: On it. Confirming egress rules to S3 and secrets manager. Any expected service accounts? @Raj
Raj: Use `svc-redwood-lon5-inference` and `kms-redwood-lon5`. I pushed iam-binding earlier.
Sam: Noted. Running basic pod health check:
Sam: ```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=redwood-nodepool -o wide
kubectl -n inference exec -it redwood-nodepool-0 -- nvidia-smi
```
Sam: Saw one node with driver mismatch (510 vs 525). I'll cordon + drain and set DRAIN_REASON.
infra-oncall: Be careful: draining will reduce starting capacity. Recommend sequential drain and add temporary burst nodes.
Mira: Also saw NTP offset ~2.1s on one host — will restart chronyd.
Alex: Keep me posted. Key SLOs: p50 < 45ms, p95 < 120ms, error rate < 0.5% under 8k qps. Run load generator against canary service: https://go/redwood/loadtest
Sam: Load test started. Initial results: p50 38ms, p95 190ms (spike), error rate 0.8% - seems NVLINK not enabled on that rack.
Raj: NVLINK firmware patch queued — applying to rack-03 now. ETA ~12m.
Mira: KMS access failed from two pods — turned out to be iptables rule blocking 443 egress to kms endpoint. Fixed.
Alex: Good catch. After fixes, re-run loadtest and full smoke script (link in runbook).
Sam: Re-ran: p50 36ms, p95 110ms, errors 0.2%. Marking readiness: partial green (autoscale + nvlink pending). :thumbsup:
Alex: OK — schedule handoff to SRE for production routing at 10:30 UTC. Leaving notes in runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/lon5
deploy-bot: rollouts/2026-05-03/lon5-nodepool -> completed (canary pass).
Lucy: I'll own the routing handoff. Joining 10:30.
Alex: Thanks all. Action items: Raj firmware, Sam drain sequence doc, Mira NTP & iptables note. Close when routing handoff done.
